The UK will provide Saudi Arabia with “defensive air-to-air refuelling” support following Houthi drone and missile attacks, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said.
The support, expected to begin in the coming days, will involve a single RAF Voyager aircraft based at RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. 
UK officials said the deployment will be “time limited” and likely last “for weeks.”
Burnham said the move followed a Saudi request for “military support” and was aimed at protecting regional stability and British interests.
“Saudi Arabia has been experiencing attacks, is looking at potential further disruption, and we need to keep those pathways open, and hence our agreement to the request.”
Source: BBC

Families demand answers after Israel killed Gaza aid workers
Families of three British World Central Kitchen workers killed in Gaza are seeking a full inquest into the Israeli drone strikes that killed them, including scrutiny of IDF targeting procedures and surveillance footage held by the UK military, Declassified UK reported.
James Henderson, James Kirby and John Chapman were among seven aid workers killed in three Israeli strikes roughly four minutes apart on April 1, 2024.
Lawyers want the coroner to determine whether the killings were unlawful and to obtain IDF drone footage, internal investigation files and targeting policies. Israel has said it will not pursue criminal investigations into the incident.
The families are also pressing Britain’s Ministry of Defence to disclose footage from an RAF surveillance aircraft that spent around five hours over Gaza that day.
💬 “There is no other independent investigation into James’ death. This inquest is all we have, and we are going to see it through,” the Kirby family said.
A second pre-inquest review is expected in March 2027.

Satellite images show damage to seven oil tanks near Riyadh airport after Houthi attack
Newly released satellite imagery indicates that at least seven oil storage tanks at a facility near King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh were damaged in recent Yemeni attacks, Press TV reported.
The imagery follows the September 19 strikes claimed by Yemen’s Ansar Allah forces against what they described as “sensitive sites” in Riyadh and Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
Reuters reported at the time that a large plume of black smoke was visible near the airport, while firefighters extinguished a blaze at a fuel tank carrying the Aramco logo. The attack also caused major delays and cancellations at King Khalid International Airport.
The strikes came amid a broader escalation between Ansar Allah and Saudi Arabia, with energy infrastructure increasingly affected by the fighting.

🇺🇸 US proposes $5B fund to rebuild Gulf energy infrastructure
The Trump administration has proposed putting $5 billion into a new fund to repair Middle Eastern energy infrastructure damaged during the Iran war and reduce regional dependence on the Strait of Hormuz, The Wall Street Journal reported.
The US wants Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Iraq and Jordan to provide matching contributions, bringing the proposed Partnership for Allied Trust and Construction (PACT) to $10 billion.
The plan is still under discussion, and it remains unclear which countries will join. Some Gulf officials reportedly consider rebuilding before a peace deal with Tehran premature, warning that new infrastructure could again become vulnerable to missile and drone strikes.
💬 “This strategy has risk written all over it,” TRENDS US managing director Bilal Saab said.
The initiative follows extensive damage to pipelines, refineries and export terminals across the region during the seven-month conflict.
